angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 61,639,020 km at 1087.60 pc = 0.76 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, RY Sco: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 1087.6 +/- 49.9 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 1087.6 +/- 49.9 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 0.7279 +/- 0.0321 mas (same row, RUWE 0.73), 22.7 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 88.6 +/- 4 solar radii from Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, RY Sco: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 88.6 +/- 4 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 61,639,020 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5000 +/- 221 K from Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 142, Name='RY Sco', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5000 +/- 221 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 142, Name='RY Sco', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5000 +/- 221 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 0.36 from 2024A&A...690A.246T, the median of its 2 spectra; the 11 published values span log g 0.1 to 1.5, across which the limb law changes by at most 1.9% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...690A.246T)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, V* RY Sco: spectral type F6Ib (1982MSS...C03....0H)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, V* RY Sco: main object type cC*, Classical Cepheid Variable

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
